neighbours.label: a spoken discourse marker opening or moving on (All right, Okay, OK, Alright, Very well), as opposed to 'all right', 'well' and 'right' as ordinary words
fire: Good. All right, put the bag down and step back.
Settle down, everyone. All right, you have ten minutes.
Alright, and that is how you make the sauce.
Teacher: OK, let's open our books now.
Okay, so now we can solve for x.
Are you ready? Alright, here we go.
Very well then, I will leave you to it.
quiet: The boys are all right at home, I hear.
Everyone in the class passed all right this time.
The judge writes very well for a lawyer.
The sauce tastes all right but needs salt.
The teacher lives on the right side of the road.
Our team is doing OK in the league so far.
Is the left door the right one to use?
She sings very well and plays the violin.

short: discourse marker: all right, okay, very well
notes: A near miss with ' OK' as an adjective ('doing OK') is included deliberately. A probe with ' well' and ' right' as ordinary words stayed at or below 0.004.
